To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Tolerance to one virus is often traded-off against tolerance against another; 2) The evolution of tolerance is mediated by the modification of plant growth, resource allocation, and mortality rates; and 3) Tolerance to TuMV and CMVs are associated with different mechanisms and trade-offs.

(1) tolerance to one virus can be traded-off with tolerance to another virus, (2) tolerance to one pathogen is associated with changes of life-history traits, (3) tolerance is a plant response that can be induced by pathogens and (4) the trade-off between tolerance to different viruses depends on pathogen virulence.
tolerance is a widespread defence strategy against viruses, and that tolerance to one virus can be traded off with tolerance to another, but not with resistance.
